title: Metr Fit for developers
description: Add product-specific size recommendations to an online store through a REST API.

blocks.text: You send your product catalog, available variants and approved size charts. Your backend requests a questionnaire, submits customer answers and receives a size recommendation with confidence, fit details and an explanation. All customer-facing requests go through your own backend.

items: One merchant can own multiple stores. Every resource is isolated by merchant and store.

Sizing runs in three modules: every chart is normalized to body centimetres, explicit answers (height, weight, tape measurements) become body estimates with stated uncertainty, and implicit answers (usual size, a size worn at another brand, body-shape illustrations) refine them. When the operator configures it, TypeSafe's Jev model then chooses among the plausible, in-stock chart sizes. Nothing can invent a size or a body measurement.
Adult tops, bottoms, dresses/one-piece garments and supported shoe charts are covered. Unsupported products return an explicit error.
Confidence is an uncalibrated evidence score, not a probability of fit or a measured accuracy claim.

blocks.text: Follow the Quickstart, then read Authentication and Integration flow before putting Fit on a product page. The API Reference below is generated from the Go route registry and wire types, not a proposed SDK.

export METR_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
# Run the API repository locally first. Use HTTPS for a deployed service.
python3 scripts/demo.py

All product endpoints use /v1. Deploy your own API from metr_api; this documentation does not imply a shared hosted endpoint. Health checks are /healthz and /readyz. The OpenAPI contract is available at /v1/openapi.json on your deployment.

title: Shopify authorization
description: Verify an app launch and authorize a shop; catalog sync and storefront sizing remain separate.

blocks.text: Set the app launch URL to https://metr.so/console and register https://metr.so/api/console/shopify/callback as the exact redirect. The API requests read_products,read_inventory. App credentials and the stable token-encryption key belong in server-side Secret Manager configuration, never in themes or browser JavaScript.

A launch without code and state is not completed authorization. The website backend sends the original signed query in a JSON body to the gateway-only endpoint below. Go verifies HMAC, shop syntax, unique query parameters and freshness. The response contains only shop; it saves no connection and creates no OAuth state.
POST /v1/console/shopify/launch

Retain the signed launch privately for at most ten minutes, require seller sign-in and explicit Metr store selection, and reverify before starting OAuth. An unsigned shop query is never proof of authorization.

The website sends launch_query in the authenticated store-specific start body, or an empty object for the ordinary flow. The backend scopes the selected store to the merchant and binds fresh single-use state to its store-domain snapshot, seller session and the verified Shopify shop. It does not silently rewrite the saved storefront domain.
POST /v1/console/stores/{store_id}/shopify/start

The callback requires Shopify HMAC, a fresh timestamp, the originating session, unexpired single-use state and an exact shop match. Only a successful token exchange with the required scopes saves AES-GCM encrypted tokens. An app launch alone cannot save a connection.
GET /v1/console/shopify/callback

items: shop_mismatch: the verified callback shop differs from the shop in this session's state. Open the app from Shopify and start a new authorization for its verified shop.
invalid_callback: callback signature, timestamp or required fields failed validation.
invalid_state: state expired, was consumed, is missing or belongs to another tenant/session.
invalid_launch: the launch signature, fields or freshness could not be verified. Open the app again from Shopify.
store_changed: the saved store domain changed during authorization.
shopify_unavailable: token exchange failed; start a fresh authorization.

blocks.text: Authorization does not import a catalog or install a sizing widget. Automatic token refresh is not implemented; expired tokens require reauthorization. Never log launch/callback queries, codes, state, credentials or tokens.

title: Your first size recommendation
description: Create a merchant, connect a store and complete one sizing session.

blocks.text: In the metr_api repository, copy .env.example to .env, replace the local database password and bootstrap key, then run docker compose up --build. Set BOOTSTRAP_KEY in your shell to the same local value. The standard-library Python example creates fictional tops, trousers, a dress and shoes, runs the quiz, accepts each recommendation and reports purchases and return/kept outcomes.

docker compose up --build
# In another terminal, load BOOTSTRAP_KEY securely from your local .env.
export METR_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
python3 scripts/demo.py

The requests below show that flow step by step. Set STORE_ID, CHART_ID, PRODUCT_ID and SESSION_ID from each response. Replace placeholder IDs inside JSON bodies before sending; single-quoted JSON does not expand shell variables.

Only the Metr operator uses the bootstrap credential. A store developer receives a merchant admin key through a secure channel; they must never receive the operator key. The response contains merchant.id and api_key.secret. Save that secret as METR_API_KEY; it is returned only once.

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "name": "Example store",
  "domain": "https://shop.example.com"
}'
Save the returned id as STORE_ID. Create a store-scoped backend key with catalog, fit and events permissions for the integration; keep the merchant admin key in your operator tooling.
This example uses full garment chest circumferences. Customer answers are body centimetres. The merchant must check the measurements before setting verified=true.

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/products" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "external_id": "linen-shirt",
  "title": "Linen camp-collar shirt",
  "product_type": "shirt",
  "gender": "unisex",
  "garment_fit": "regular",
  "stretch": "none",
  "size_chart_id": "REPLACE_WITH_CHART_ID"
}'

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/products/$PRODUCT_ID/variants" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "external_id": "shirt-m-black",
  "size": "M",
  "color": "black",
  "available": true
}'
Create S and L variants in the same way if they are available. Save the product id as PRODUCT_ID. Variant sizes must exactly match chart labels.

sections.title: 5. Request the questionnaire and start a session

blocks.text:
curl --fail-with-body -X GET "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/products/$PRODUCT_ID/fit-questionnaire" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY"

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/fit-sessions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "product_id": "REPLACE_WITH_PRODUCT_ID",
  "color": "black",
  "customer_reference": "opaque-customer-reference"
}'
Use the questionnaire returned by session creation to render the quiz. It is frozen with that session’s chart revision. Save id as SESSION_ID.

Send the answers so far and any skipped question IDs. The response is either the next question to show or done=true, with the current estimate. Repeat until done; the quiz asks the question that most reduces uncertainty about the size and stops once one size is clearly most likely.
The response includes recommended_size, per-size probabilities, eligible variant_ids, confidence, per-area fit, method and explanation. Render the result and let the customer choose.

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/fit-sessions/$SESSION_ID/complete" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "decision": "accepted",
  "chosen_variant_id": "REPLACE_WITH_RECOMMENDED_VARIANT_ID"
}'

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "external_id": "order-123-line-1-purchase",
  "source": "custom-store",
  "type": "purchase",
  "product_id": "REPLACE_WITH_PRODUCT_ID",
  "variant_id": "REPLACE_WITH_PURCHASED_VARIANT_ID",
  "session_id": "REPLACE_WITH_SESSION_ID",
  "order_id": "order-123",
  "line_item_id": "line-1",
  "quantity": 1,
  "occurred_at": "REPLACE_WITH_CURRENT_RFC3339_TIMESTAMP"
}'
Purchase events come from your backend after a confirmed order. Include the same product, order and line IDs on later returns or exchanges. The demo supplies current timestamps automatically.

title: Authentication and store isolation
description: Keep Metr credentials on your server and use the smallest scope each integration needs.

rows: POST /v1/merchants only. Stored outside merchant integrations.
Create stores, manage keys and access the merchant’s resources.
Only its named store and granted scopes. Never another store.

blocks.text: Authorization: Bearer YOUR_SECRET_API_KEY
API keys are returned once and stored as SHA-256 digests. There is no login endpoint or token refresh flow. Create a replacement key before revoking an old key.

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/api-keys" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "name": "Store integration",
  "store_id": "REPLACE_WITH_STORE_ID",
  "scopes": [
    "catalog",
    "fit",
    "events",
    "analytics"
  ]
}'

rows: Merchant administration, or resource administration limited to a named store. Store-bound admin cannot issue keys or create stores.
Products, variants, size charts and product types.

blocks.text: Non-admin keys must specify store_id. Optional expires_at must be a future RFC3339 timestamp within one year. Key issuance and listing require an unrestricted merchant admin key.

curl --fail-with-body -X DELETE "$METR_API_URL/v1/api-keys/$KEY_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY"
Revoked keys immediately receive 401. A key cannot revoke itself. Create or use another admin key for rotation.

Do not put secret keys in themes, browser JavaScript, mobile apps, URLs or analytics. Your backend must authorize the customer’s session before forwarding answers. Validate webhook signatures in your integration before forwarding purchase/return events. The optional seller console supports accounts, store-scoped keys and Shopify OAuth authorization. Shopify catalog sync, storefront proxy and outcome webhooks are not implemented yet.

title: Products and variants
description: Tell Metr which item is being sized and which sizes are available to buy.

blocks.text:
curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/products" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "external_id": "linen-shirt",
  "title": "Linen camp-collar shirt",
  "product_type": "shirt",
  "gender": "unisex",
  "garment_fit": "regular",
  "stretch": "none",
  "size_chart_id": "cht_example"
}'

rows: Your catalog identifier; unique within a store, up to 128 characters.
women, men or unisex. Adult product metadata, not a customer inference.
none, moderate or high. Not an invented stretch percentage.
An approved, category-compatible chart from the same store.

blocks.text: accessory is recognized but does not support recommendations. Children’s products, bras and separately sized multi-piece sets need a different model and are not supported by V1.

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/products/$PRODUCT_ID/variants" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "external_id": "linen-shirt-M",
  "size": "M",
  "color": "black",
  "available": true
}'

A variant ID belongs to one product, merchant and store. Size labels match chart rows exactly, including case. Multiple colors can share one size. Send color when starting a session to recommend only variants of that color.

Use PUT on the product or variant resource to replace its documented input fields. Set available=false as soon as a variant is unavailable. Variant size and color are immutable; create a new variant if either changes. Chart-backed recommendations never invent a size that is absent from current available inventory. An already-returned recommendation is historical, so recheck stock before adding to cart.

List endpoints return data and optional next_cursor. Use ?limit=50&cursor=LAST_CURSOR. The maximum page size is 100. Creation is not generally idempotent: use your external_id and the list/get/PUT flow to reconcile interrupted catalog syncs.

title: Size charts and measurements
description: Explicit units and measurement definitions prevent ambiguous size matching.

rows: cm or in. The engine normalizes both to centimetres.
body = body-size range; garment = actual garment dimensions.
circumference, flat_width or linear, declared per measurement.
Only garment chest, waist, hips and thigh; doubled to circumference.
Shoulders, sleeve, length, rise, inseam and foot length; never doubled.
1–30 unique sizes, ordered smallest to largest by primary measurements.
Set true only after the merchant checks the chart. Draft charts cannot generate recommendations.
Optional. A verified chart with share_as_reference=true and a brand name is offered to every store's customers as “which size fits you at <brand>?”. Only the brand, sizes and measurements are shared.

blocks.text: Every row must contain every declared measurement. min and max form an inclusive range; equal values describe one measurement. Do not send an image or HTML table: normalize the approved values first.

A chart’s category must match the product type. Footwear uses a body foot-length chart; a shoe’s outside dimensions are not a body measurement. Charts missing primary body areas are rejected. The API validates structure and ranges, but merchant verification is still required to establish that the values describe the actual garment.

PUT /v1/stores/{store_id}/size-charts/{chart_id} replaces the input fields and increments revision. Category cannot change. Existing sessions retain their original chart snapshot; new sessions use the new revision. Sizes removed from a chart will no longer be candidates for new sessions.

title: Adaptive questionnaires
description: Ask each customer only the questions that help for this product.

blocks.text:
curl --fail-with-body -X GET "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/products/$PRODUCT_ID/fit-questionnaire" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY"

Optional ?color=black restricts available_sizes to that exact variant color. Session creation returns the frozen questionnaire (version fit-quiz-2.0.0) to use for actual answers. Every question is optional.

Use id as the answer key, label as the visible question, option_labels (when present) as display text for options, and min/max/unit for numbers. Question IDs beginning measurements. map into the answers.measurements object.

The response is {done, question, asked, estimate}. Show question, add the answer (or its ID to skipped) and call again. The quiz asks explicit inputs first when something uses them, then the question with the largest expected reduction in size uncertainty. A tape measurement must be worth twice a click. It stops when one size has at least 0.8 of the probability, nothing useful remains, or ten questions were asked. Then submit the answers for a recommendation.

items: explicit: body_track (only for unisex apparel; picks the illustration set), height_cm, weight_kg and age. Product type and gender come from the product.
sizes: usual_size at this brand, reference_size at another brand that shares its chart, and size_consistency.
fit: preferred_fit (close, regular or loose) for apparel.

body_shape: silhouette_shoulders, silhouette_waist, silhouette_hips and silhouette_thigh, answered with a fashion_sizing_assets illustration such as female_tops_waist_stomach:3. They describe shape for Jev and never become centimetres. They are asked only when Jev is enabled.
measurements: optional body tape measurements in centimetres for chart areas. Garment-only lengths are not asked.
Footwear asks only usual size, reference size, consistency and foot length.

blocks.text: A session starts with POST /fit-sessions and expires after 24 hours. The API records fit_started. Submitting valid answers and receiving a recommendation records fit_completed and recommendation_generated atomically. A customer can redo the quiz by creating a new session.

title: Size recommendations
description: Submit answers once and return the recommended size, supporting evidence and limitations.

blocks.text: variant_ids contains currently available variants matching the recommended chart size and session color. Fit is unknown for body areas without a supplied measurement. Body charts describe below_range, within_range or above_range; garment charts describe the estimated ease or length relationship.

probabilities spreads belief over the available sizes. confidence is the chosen size's probability, clamped to 0.15–0.90 (0.60 without a tape measurement or reference brand). It is an uncalibrated evidence score, not the probability a size will fit. method is rules, or rules+jev when Jev chose among the plausible sizes. If Jev is unavailable the rules estimate is returned with a warning. Do not turn confidence into a ‘91% accurate’ claim.

curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/fit-sessions/$SESSION_ID/complete" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "decision": "accepted",
  "chosen_variant_id": "var_medium"
}'

items: accepted: selected variant has the recommended size.
overridden: selected variant has a different available size for the same product and session color.
declined: no chosen_variant_id; the customer did not select a recommendation.

blocks.text: Identical recommendation retries return the same persisted response. Changed answers return 409: start another session. Identical completion retries are also safe. Recommendations do not reserve stock. Recheck availability before adding to cart. On no_suitable_size, missing approval, insufficient evidence, timeout or an unavailable service, show the merchant’s size chart and keep checkout available.

title: Events and commercial outcomes
description: Connect quiz behavior to later order outcomes without claiming that correlation proves impact.

rows: Session completed with the recommended size.
Session completed with a different size.

blocks.text: Do not send these to POST /events; the API records them transactionally. This prevents retries from inflating quiz and decision counts.

items: fit_viewed: the customer sees the size-help entry point.
add_to_cart and checkout_started: send from the storefront integration through your backend.
purchase: send from the backend after a confirmed order.
return_requested and size_exchange: include reason=size or other.
item_kept: an explicit verified signal; never infer it from missing return data.

blocks.text:
curl --fail-with-body -X POST "$METR_API_URL/v1/stores/$STORE_ID/events" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $METR_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
  "external_id": "order-123-line-1-return",
  "source": "custom-store",
  "type": "return_requested",
  "product_id": "prd_example",
  "variant_id": "var_medium",
  "session_id": "fit_example",
  "order_id": "order-123",
  "line_item_id": "line-1",
  "reason": "size",
  "quantity": 1,
  "occurred_at": "REPLACE_WITH_CURRENT_RFC3339_TIMESTAMP"
}'

Use stable external_id values for deliveries. The uniqueness boundary is merchant + store + source + external_id. Identical retries return 200 and the original event; changed payloads return 409. First delivery returns 201. occurred_at must be within the previous year and no more than five minutes ahead.

Order outcomes require product_id, variant_id, order_id and line_item_id. Keep order/line IDs stable across purchase, return, exchange and kept signals. session_id is optional for unassisted purchases and delayed outcomes, but include it on a Fit-assisted purchase. If supplied, it must belong to the same product and store. Never attach an event that predates the session.

GET /v1/stores/{store_id}/metrics accepts from/to RFC3339 timestamps. It selects sessions created in [from,to) and observes linked outcomes through the response’s observed_through time. Maximum range: 366 days. Default: last 30 days. Metrics count unique sessions and purchased order lines, not units.

rows: Recommended sessions with a linked purchase / recommended sessions
Purchased lines with a size return / Fit-assisted purchased lines
Purchased lines with an explicit kept signal / Fit-assisted purchased lines
Purchased lines with a size exchange / Fit-assisted purchased lines

blocks.text: A zero denominator returns null. Return and kept windows may be immature, and missing integration events bias rates. Different outcomes may apply to one line over time. These descriptive cohorts do not establish causal conversion lift or return reduction. Use a properly designed randomized experiment for causal claims.

title: Errors and recovery
description: Every API error includes a stable code, a readable message and a request ID.

rows: Malformed JSON, duplicate/unknown fields, or invalid query. Fix the request.
Missing, revoked or expired API key.
Key lacks the scope or is restricted to a different store.
Resource does not exist inside this tenant/store.
Wrong HTTP method; check Allow header.
Duplicate identifier, conflicting retry or invalid session transition.
Session expired; create a new one.
Invalid values, chart mismatch or sizing abstention. Show a chart fallback where appropriate.
Rate limited. Respect Retry-After; default is 300 requests/minute/key.
Internal/dependency failure. Retry safe operations with bounded backoff.

items: unsupported_product: this category is not supported.
unverified_chart: attach and approve a chart first.
no_available_sizes: no current variants match chart rows and chosen color.
insufficient_evidence: provide a usual size, a size worn at another brand or a body measurement.
invalid_answers: an answer is invalid or irrelevant for this product.
no_suitable_size: the available sizes are too poor a match; do not force a size.

blocks.text: GET operations, identical recommendation/completion requests and identical event deliveries can be retried. Merchant/product/chart/session creation does not have automatic idempotency: reconcile state before retrying. Retry-After is returned for 429. Keep the request ID for support; never log API keys or body measurements.

title: API reference
description: The complete REST contract, generated from the implementation.

blocks.text: The operation list, request schemas and response schemas below are generated from the API’s route registry and Go wire types. Download the OpenAPI 3.1 document to import it into your client generator or API tool. Replace the local server URL with your own deployed API.

items: Bearer authentication uses operator or merchant/store keys as indicated per operation.
All bodies are JSON objects; unknown and duplicate fields are rejected.
Lists use limit (1–100) and cursor, returning data and optional next_cursor.
IDs are opaque. Never derive tenant identity from a request body.
PUT replaces the documented input fields; it is not a partial PATCH.
The request body maximum is 256 KiB. API version: /v1.

title: Integrate Fit into your store
description: Keep customer authorization, inventory and order truth in your ecommerce backend.

blocks.text: Obtain a merchant key, create a store and issue store-scoped backend keys. Sync products, verified charts and variants. Maintain stable external identifiers and keep availability current. Complete the Quickstart with fictional data before connecting a real store.

sections.title: 2. Put the quiz on the product page

blocks.text: Render a ‘Find my size’ entry point and report fit_viewed through your backend. When the customer starts, create a session for the product and chosen color. Save its ID in that customer’s server-side session and render the returned questions. Do not expose your Metr key to the browser.

Submit only advertised answers, then show the returned size, explanation and available variants. Treat unknown fit areas as unknown. Offer the size chart and a redo action. Starting over creates a new session rather than rewriting historical answers.

Complete the session as accepted, overridden or declined. Check stock before adding to cart. Store the fit_session_id with the cart/order line so your order backend can report later outcomes. Fit does not process carts, payments or shipping.

Send confirmed purchases and subsequent returns/exchanges/kept signals from trusted backend events. Validate ecommerce-platform webhook signatures in your adapter and reuse stable delivery IDs. Unassisted orders can omit session_id. Do not build attribution from a customer name or an email address.

Use timeouts, bounded retries and the merchant’s size chart as fallback. A sizing outage must not block checkout. Agree consent and retention with the merchant. V1 provides an explicit pruning script for body answers and pseudonymous references; backups and exports need the same approved policy.

The optional seller console supports account signup/login, store creation, scoped keys and Shopify OAuth authorization. It is not a complete Shopify app: automatic catalog sync, the storefront widget, token refresh and outcome webhooks remain pending. No JavaScript SDK, payment flow or Discover API ships with Fit V1.
